gen-eater-fs-chillax: Dark, aggressive display lettering, with Eater putting generous gaps between its characters. And Chillax, with a line like spaghetti and loops left unfinished, keeps a long paragraph relaxed and casual.
gen-eater-fs-plein: Dark, aggressive and widely spaced: that is Eater in a nutshell. Plein takes over with a clear channel leading in to the round shapes, so a page of text stays reliable and clean.
gen-eater-fs-synonym: Synonym draws its strokes like a stitched thread outline, with generous openings in every curve that keep the text clean and dependable. Underneath Eater's dark shouting, paragraphs settle into a smooth, steady read.
gen-eater-gf-aclonica: Eater packs hairline-free strokes and a dark, aggressive bite. Aclonica stretches out beneath it in a long, widely spaced line, with a deep midsection and a shift in thickness you feel more than see.
gen-eater-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters and ascenders kept short. Alumni Sans SC squeezes its letters together, with oversized lowercase that makes paragraphs feel compact and contemporary.
gen-eater-gf-arsenal: Thin strokes with no hairlines give Eater a dark, aggressive edge. And Arsenal, a sans with a close-knit string of letters and a modest weight shift, steadies the page beneath it.
gen-eater-gf-asimovian: Mild contrast, never stark, gives Eater its dark, aggressive snarl. But Asimovian traces every letter with a line of constant weight, and its lowercase bodies run deep, which makes a friendly counterweight.
gen-eater-gf-cal-sans: Eater delivers drama, with moderate swings in line thickness and a dark, aggressive mood. Cal Sans does the opposite job, its tubular strokes like bent copper pipe staying friendly and modern in running text.
gen-eater-gf-days-one: Days One reads like rungs on a rope ladder, its spacing steady and its lowercase filling the line top to bottom. Eater brings sturdy hairlines and a dark mood over that sans.
gen-eater-gf-epunda-sans: Eater brings a dark, aggressive mood, with moderate contrast that reads easily. And Epunda Sans, with oversized e and a counters and curves full of daylight, makes openness the best thing about this pairing.
